setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart holding a barbell or EZ-bar in an overhand grip about shoulder width.
Let the bar rest against your thighs at arm's length, brace your trunk and set your shoulders down and back.
steps: Drive the elbows up and out to the sides so the bar travels straight up along your body.
Stop when the bar reaches the lower chest and your upper arms are about level with the floor, elbows above the wrists.
Hold for a moment, then lower the bar along the same path until your arms are straight again.
Repeat for the planned number of reps without swinging the torso.
instructions.breathing: Exhale as the bar rises and inhale as you lower it under control.

common_faults.fault: Pulling the bar up to the chin with the elbows above shoulder height
common_faults.correction: Finish the pull at the lower chest with the upper arms level with the floor, which keeps the shoulder out of the pinch range.

common_faults.fault: Rocking back and heaving the bar with the hips
common_faults.correction: Lighten the load, keep the trunk still and let the shoulders and elbows do the lifting.

common_faults.fault: Letting the wrists curl up as the bar rises
common_faults.correction: Keep the wrists straight and think of the hands as hooks so the elbows stay highest.

precautions: The shoulder-width grip puts the shoulder in more internal rotation than a wide grip; if the front of the shoulder pinches, widen the grip, shorten the range or switch to an EZ-bar.

name: Barbell Upright Row
summary: A standing vertical pull with a shoulder-width overhand grip on a barbell, lifting the bar along the torso to the lower chest to work the side deltoids and upper trapezius.
